message:
fix: the stripper was truncating real photographs — DRI must survive

LIVE DEFECT #3, fast path. The founder's captured photo rendered as a strip of
real image over flat grey — the signature of a decode that stops part-way — and
stripJpegMetadata is the only thing rewriting those bytes.

A CONTRADICTION INSIDE ONE FILE: nextEntropyMarker deliberately walks past
RST0-RST7, so the code already knew restart markers occur in these streams,
while isAllowedHeaderSegment dropped DRI — the segment that declares the restart
interval — and the comment listed it as deleted by name. A decoder meeting a
restart marker it was never told about stops there.

NOT A PREVIEW BUG: the preview URI is built from the stripped bytes precisely so
what he sees is what uploads, so the same truncation was going into heroSquare,
heroVertical, proof and detail. The WYSIWYG law is what made it visible; without
it this reaches a vitrine.

WHY THE SUITE MISSED IT: every fixture has a hand-built entropy stream with no
restart interval. The stripper was only tested against JPEGs we wrote ourselves,
never one written the way a phone encoder writes them.

FIX: DRI admitted to the allow-list. Two bytes of restart count — rendering
structure like DQT/DHT/SOF, no user data — and the privacy property is re-checked
on the same stream. Red-proven: removing the line fails the decodability test.

NOT PROVEN, STATED: there is no real JPEG encoder in this environment, so the fix
is verified against a synthetic stream that now carries restart markers, not
against a photograph from his phone. The proof is his next capture rendering
whole. The real gap — the imaging path has never met one real camera JPEG — is
named, not filled.

VERIFIED: typecheck 11/11 · supplier-app 467/467 (37 files) · ALL GATES GREEN.
